**WD-2: I can select necessary columns from a dataset.**

-   Example selecting specified columns

```{r}
#| label: wd-2-ex-1
# Lab 3 Question 5, revised
# Revision made the select function more condensed making use of :
teacher_evals_clean <- Teacher_Eval |>
  filter(no_participants > 9) |>
  rename(sex = gender)|>
  mutate(teacher_id = as.character(teacher_id),
         course_id = as.character(course_id)) |>
  select(course_id:SET_score_avg,
         percent_failed_cur,
         academic_degree:sex)
```

-   Example removing specified columns

```{r}
#| label: wd-2-ex-2
# Lab 9 question 6
evals |>
    distinct(teacher_id,
           .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    mutate('Academic Degree' = fct_recode(academic_degree,
             'No Degree' = 'no_dgr',
             'Masters' = 'ma',
             'Doctorate' = 'dr',
             'Tenured Professor' = 'prof'),
         'Seniority' =  case_when(
              seniority <= 4 ~ 'Junior',
              seniority >= 5 & seniority <= 8 ~ 'Senior',
              seniority >= 9 ~ 'Very Senior'),
         'Sex' = fct_recode(sex,
              'Male' = 'male',
              'Female' = 'female')
         ) |>
    select(-c(matches('^[[:lower:]]', ignore.case = F), starts_with('SET'))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = 'variable',
               values_to = 'level') |>
    count(variable, level) |>
    group_by(variable) |>
    mutate(prop = n/sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    gt(rowname_col = 'level',
       groupname_col = 'variable') |>
    cols_label(variable = md('**Demographic**'),
               level = md('**Group**'),
               n = md('**Count**'),
               prop = md('**%**')) |>
    tab_header(
    title = 'Demographics of Professors',
    subtitle = 'Student Evaluations at the University of Poland, Warsaw in 2020') |>
    tab_spanner(label = md('**Professors**'),
                columns = c(n, prop)) |>
    fmt_percent(columns = prop,
                decimals = 2) |>
    tab_options(row_group.background.color = 'grey',
                row_group.font.weight = 'bold')
```

-   Factor Example 1 (renaming levels)

```{r}
#| label: wd-4-factor-ex-1
# Lab 4 Question 7 Revised
# Feedback: Can you get your facet labels to be the same as mine? Can you reorder the facets so they go in the same order as mine?

#Can you reorder the colors in the legend so they appear in the same order as the lines in the plot? I am specifically looking for a tool that does the reordering for you since doing the reordering by hand is not a robust programming practice!

#I like your colors! Can you find which ones I used?

# Revision: Reordered factors, added brewer.pal to match the colors
match_colors = colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Accent"))(10)

ca_childcare |>
  select(Region, study_year, mc_infant, mc_toddler, mc_preschool) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = mc_infant:mc_preschool,
    names_to = "Ages",
    values_to = "Weekly_Median") |>
    mutate(Ages = fct_recode(Ages,
                  "Infant"    = "mc_infant",
                  "Toddler"   = "mc_toddler",
                  "Preschool" = "mc_preschool"),
            Ages = factor(Ages, levels = c("Infant", "Toddler", "Preschool")),
            Region = fct_reorder2(Region,
                                  study_year,
                                  Weekly_Median))|>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = study_year,
                       y = Weekly_Median,
                       color = Region)) +
           geom_point() +
           geom_smooth() +
           facet_wrap(~Ages) +
  scale_color_manual(values = match_colors) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1,
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = 'bold')) +
  labs(x = 'Study Year',
       y = '',
       title = 'Weekly Median Price for Center-Based Childcare (USD)',
       color = 'California Region') +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018),
                     labels = c(2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency(prefix = '$'))
```

-   Character (example must use functions from **stringr**)

```{r}
#| label: wd-4-string
# Lab 8 Question 3
density_plot_func <- function(df, quant_var, cat_var){
  x_lab = str_to_title(
    str_replace_all(string = rlang::englue('{{quant_var}}'),
                    pattern = '_',
                    replacement = ' '))
  by_lab = str_to_title(
    str_replace_all(string = rlang::englue('{{cat_var}}'),
                    pattern = '_',
                    replacement = ' '))
  title_lab = rlang::englue('Density Plot of {x_lab} separated by {by_lab}')
  
  df |>
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = {{quant_var}},
                         fill = {{cat_var}})) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5,
                 na.rm = TRUE) +
    labs(x = x_lab,
         y = 'Density',
         title = title_lab,
         fill = by_lab)
}


```

**WD-6: I can use filtering joins to filter rows from a dataframe.**

-   `semi_join()`

```{r}
#| label: wd-6-semi
# Lab 5 Following up on testimonies
# Revised to use semi join to filter data
follow_up_witness_1 <- get_fit_now_member |>
  filter(str_detect(id, '^48Z'),
         membership_status == 'gold')

follow_up_witness_2 <- get_fit_now_check_in |>
  mutate(check_in_date = ymd(check_in_date)) |>
  filter(check_in_date == '2018/01/09') |>
  semi_join(follow_up_witness_1, by = join_by(membership_id == id)) |>
  left_join(follow_up_witness_1, by = join_by(membership_id == id)) |>
  left_join(person, by = join_by(person_id == id))
  
witness_testimonies_follow_up <- drivers_license |>
  filter(str_detect(plate_number, 'H42W')) |>
  semi_join(follow_up_witness_2, join_by(id == license_id))

witness_testimonies_follow_up
```

-   `anti_join()`

```{r}
#| label: wd-6-anti
# Lab 5 Following up on Shooters Claim
# Added the bottom chunk of code to answer the question "how many times did people who dont drive a Model S and not around 65-67" and dont have red hair?". 
#| label: follow-up-on-shooters-claim
possible_car <- drivers_license |>
  filter(car_make == 'Tesla',
         car_model == 'Model S',
         hair_color == 'red',
         between(height, 65, 67))

potential_hirers <- person |>
  semi_join(possible_car, by = join_by(license_id == id))

  facebook_event_checkin |>
  semi_join(potential_hirers, by = join_by(person_id == id)) |>
  left_join(potential_hirers, by = c("person_id" = "id")) |>
  mutate(date = ymd(date)) |>
  select(name, event_name, date) |>
  filter(month(date) == 12,
         year(date) == 2017,
         event_name == 'SQL Symphony Concert') |>
  group_by(name) |>
  count(event_name)
  
  non_hirer_concert_counts <- facebook_event_checkin |>
  mutate(date = ymd(date)) |>
  filter(month(date) == 12,
        year(date) == 2017,
        event_name == "SQL Symphony Concert") |>
  anti_join(potential_hirers, by = join_by(person_id == id)) |>
  left_join(person, by = join_by(person_id == id)) |>

```

```{r}
#| label: r-2-1
# Challenge 4 Graph
ca_childcare |>
group_by(Region, study_year) |>
  summarize(Overall_avg_Family_Cost = (mean(mfcc_infant) +
                               mean(mfcc_toddler) +
                               mean(mfcc_preschool)) / 3,
    Overall_avg_Center_Cost = (mean(mc_infant) +
                               mean(mc_toddler) +
                               mean(mc_preschool)) / 3,
    .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Overall_avg_Family_Cost,

  facet_wrap(~ study_year) +
  labs(
  title = 'As Household Income Increases, Center-Based Infant Care Becomes More Expensive',
  subtitle = 'Average weekly costs (children aged 0–54 months) by region and study year',
  x = 'Average Weekly Family Childcare Cost',
  y = 'Average Weekly Center-Based Childcare Cost',

  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = 'Set3') +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency(prefix = '$')) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency(prefix = '$'))
```

-   Example of function formatting

```{r}
#| label: r-2-3
# Lab 7 Question 5
rescale_01 <- function(x){
  if(is.numeric(x) & length(x) > 1){
    (x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / 
           (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(x, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
  else{
    stop('Error: input is non-numeric or input vecotr is not greater than 1')
  }
}
```

```{r}
                               mean(mfcc_preschool)) / 3,
    Overall_avg_Center_Cost = (mean(mc_infant) +
                               mean(mc_toddler) +
                               mean(mc_preschool)) / 3,
    .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Overall_avg_Family_Cost,
                       y = Overall_avg_Center_Cost,
                       color = Region)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ study_year) +
  labs(
  title = 'As Household Income Increases, Center-Based Infant Care Becomes More Expensive',
  subtitle = 'Average weekly costs (children aged 0–54 months) by region and study year',
  x = 'Average Weekly Family Childcare Cost',
  y = 'Average Weekly Center-Based Childcare Cost',
  color = "California Region") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = 'Set3') +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency(prefix = '$')) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency(prefix = '$'))
```

```{r}
#| label: dvs-3-3
# Lab 7 Question 3
Missing_values_by_year_trip_section <- Fish_data |>
  group_by(year, trip, section) |>
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric), Count_missing_vals)) |>
  mutate(Missing_values = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) |>
  select(year, trip, section, Missing_values)
  
Missing_values_by_year_trip_section |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = Missing_values),
              fill = "#FA8072",
              alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Missing_values),
            color = "#FA5067",
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = Missing_values),
              color = "#800000",
              method = 'lm',
              se = FALSE) +
  labs( title = "<span style='color:#FA8072;'>Number of Missing Values</span> by Year",
        subtitle = "Each Panel Shows Total Missing Observations by Trip and Section",
        y = "Missing Values",
        x = "Year") +
  facet_grid(trip ~ section) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown())
```

**DVS-4: I can calculate numerical summaries of variables.**

-   Example using `summarize()`

```{r}
#| label: dvs-4-summarize
# Lab 7 Question 1
# Summarizes the amount of missing values for each variable and how many rows have missing values
Count_missing_vals <- function(x){
  sum(is.na(x))
}

missing_vals_per_var <- Fish_data |>
  summarize(across(everything(), Count_missing_vals)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Missing_Values")

rows_with_missing_values <- Fish_data |>
  mutate(any_na = if_any(everything(), is.na)) |>
  summarize(
    Variable = "Rows with Missing Values",
    Missing_Values = sum(any_na))

  Missing_values_table <-
    bind_rows(missing_vals_per_var, rows_with_missing_values)
  
  Missing_values_table
```

-   Example using `across()`

```{r}
#| label: dvs-4-across
# Lab 7 Question 3
# computes missing value counts for each numeric variable within each year-trip-section group
Missing_values_by_year_trip_section <- Fish_data |>
  group_by(year, trip, section) |>
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric), Count_missing_vals)) |>
  mutate(Missing_values = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))) |>
  select(year, trip, section, Missing_values)
  
Missing_values_by_year_trip_section |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = Missing_values),
              fill = "#FA8072",
              alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Missing_values),
            color = "#FA5067",
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = Missing_values),
              color = "#800000",
              method = 'lm',
              se = FALSE) +
  labs( title = "<span style='color:#FA8072;'>Number of Missing Values</span> by Year",
        subtitle = "Each Panel Shows Total Missing Observations by Trip and Section",
        y = "Missing Values",
        x = "Year") +
  facet_grid(trip ~ section) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(plot.title = element_markdown())
```

```{r}
  group_by(Region, study_year) |>
  summarize(median_income = median(mhi_2018),
```

-   I can modify the text in my table to be more readable (e.g., bold face for column headers)

```{r}
#| label: dvs-6-ex-2
# Lab 9 Question 6
evals |>
    distinct(teacher_id,
           .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    mutate('Academic Degree' = fct_recode(academic_degree,
             'No Degree' = 'no_dgr',
             'Masters' = 'ma',
             'Doctorate' = 'dr',
             'Tenured Professor' = 'prof'),
         'Seniority' =  case_when(
              seniority <= 4 ~ 'Junior',
              seniority >= 5 & seniority <= 8 ~ 'Senior',
              seniority >= 9 ~ 'Very Senior'),
         'Sex' = fct_recode(sex,
              'Male' = 'male',
              'Female' = 'female')
         ) |>
    select(-c(matches('^[[:lower:]]', ignore.case = F), starts_with('SET'))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = 'variable',
               values_to = 'level') |>
    count(variable, level) |>
    group_by(variable) |>
    mutate(prop = n/sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    gt(rowname_col = 'level',
       groupname_col = 'variable') |>
    cols_label(variable = md('**Demographic**'),
               level = md('**Group**'),
               n = md('**Count**'),
               prop = md('**%**')) |>
    tab_header(
    title = 'Demographics of Professors',
    subtitle = 'Student Evaluations at the University of Poland, Warsaw in 2020') |>
    tab_spanner(label = md('**Professors**'),
                columns = c(n, prop)) |>
    fmt_percent(columns = prop,
                decimals = 2) |>
    tab_options(row_group.background.color = 'grey',
                row_group.font.weight = 'bold')
```

```{r}
#| label: dvs-6-ex-3
# Lab 4 Question 5
ca_childcare |>
  filter(study_year %in% c(2008, 2018)) |>
  group_by(Region, study_year) |>
  summarize(median_income = median(mhi_2018),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = study_year,
              values_from = median_income,
              names_prefix = "Median income from ") |>
  arrange(desc(`Median income from 2018`))
```

```{r}
evals |>
    distinct(teacher_id,

         'Seniority' =  case_when(

         'Sex' = fct_recode(sex,

              'Female' = 'female')
         ) |>
    select(-c(matches('^[[:lower:]]', ignore.case = F), starts_with('SET'))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = 'variable',
               values_to = 'level') |>
    count(variable, level) |>
    group_by(variable) |>
    mutate(prop = n/sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    gt(rowname_col = 'level',
       groupname_col = 'variable') |>
    cols_label(variable = md('**Demographic**'),
               level = md('**Group**'),
               n = md('**Count**'),
               prop = md('**%**')) |>
    tab_header(
    title = 'Demographics of Professors',
    subtitle = 'Student Evaluations at the University of Poland, Warsaw in 2020') |>
    tab_spanner(label = md('**Professors**'),
                columns = c(n, prop)) |>
    fmt_percent(columns = prop,
                decimals = 2) |>
    tab_options(row_group.background.color = 'grey',
                row_group.font.weight = 'bold')
```

**PE-2: I can write functions to reduce repetition in my code.**

-   Example 1: Function that operates on vectors

```{r}
#| label: pe-2-1
# Lab 7 Question 4
rescale_01 <- function(x){
  if(is.numeric(x) & length(x) > 1){
    (x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / 
           (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(x, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
  else{
    stop('Error: input is non-numeric or input vecotr is not greater than 1')
  }
}
```

-   Example 2: Function that operates on data frames

```{r}
#| label: pe-2-2
# Lab 8 Question 3
density_plot_func <- function(df, quant_var, cat_var){
  x_lab = str_to_title(
    str_replace_all(string = rlang::englue('{{quant_var}}'),
                    pattern = '_',
                    replacement = ' '))
  by_lab = str_to_title(
    str_replace_all(string = rlang::englue('{{cat_var}}'),
                    pattern = '_',
                    replacement = ' '))
  title_lab = rlang::englue('Density Plot of {x_lab} separated by {by_lab}')
  
  df |>
    ggplot(mapping = aes(x = {{quant_var}},
                         fill = {{cat_var}})) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5,
                 na.rm = TRUE) +
    labs(x = x_lab,
         y = 'Density',
         title = title_lab,
         fill = by_lab)
}

```

```{r}
                values_from = n,
                values_fill = 0) |>

}
```

## Data Simulation & Statisical Models

**DSSM-1: I can simulate data from a *variety* of probability models.**

-   Example 1

```{r}
#| label: dsm-1-1
# Lab 10 Question 8 & 10
mycifun <- function(beta0, beta1, n){

intercept = beta0
slope = beta1

x = runif(n, min = 0, max = 1)

ep = rnorm(n, 0, 1)

y = intercept + x*slope + ep

lm_data = tibble(x, y)

linear_model_lm = lm(y ~ x,
                     data = lm_data)

tidy(linear_model_lm,
     conf.int = T,
     conf.level = 0.95) |>
  filter(term == 'x') |>
  select(estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  mutate(cover = if_else(condition = slope >= conf.low & slope <= conf.high,
                         true = 1,
                         false = 0))

}

ci_dat <- map(.x = 1:1000,
              .f = ~ mycifun(3, 0.5, 100)
              )
```

-   Example 2

```{r}
#| label: dsm-1-2
# Lab 10 Question 1 & 2
randomBabies <- function(n_babies){
  
  baby_data <- tibble(parent = 1:n_babies,
    baby = sample(1:n_babies,
                  size = n_babies,
                  replace = F))
  
  matches <- baby_data |>
    mutate(match = ifelse(parent == baby, 1, 0)) |>
    filter(match == 1) |>
    nrow()
  
  matches
}

results <- map_int(.x = 1:10000,
                   .f = ~ randomBabies(n_babies = 4))
```

I feel that a lot of my revisions throughout the course have less to do with answering the problem but rather how I approach solving the problem. Often times when I first submit labs and challenge I can get the desired result, but my process isn't great. I believe a lot of this has to do with how I am as a person, I'm always tempted to get stuff over with, my brain only focuses on the desired output and not about how I can make the output process cleaner or more robust. My revisions mainly correspond with feedback given on my original submissions of labs and challenges. Most of the revisions I did have to do with displaying data in a nicer fashion, and I believe now after receiving feedback on what to improve on with my graphing skills I feel confident about making better graphs on future assignments.
